source.titleEnglish: Usted or Tú: Coach a Friend at a Casa Particular
source.objectiveEnglish: Explain when to switch between usted and tú, then model it with the host, her grandson and an older guest.
source.speakingEnglish: You are coaching your friend Marcus, and the AI plays Marcus, host señora Odalys, her grandson Yandiel and guest don Rigoberto: explain when to use usted or tú, then model each with softeners like quisiera, ¿me podría…? and ¿te importa…?

sourceGrammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿me podría…?, ¿te importa…?)

examples.es: Señora Odalys, ¿me podría pasar la cafetera, por favor?
examples.en: Señora Odalys, could you pass me the coffee pot, please?

examples.es: Yandiel, ¿te importa si me siento aquí?
examples.en: Yandiel, do you mind if I sit here?

titleFrenchDraft: Vouvoyer ou tutoyer dans une casa particular à Trinidad
focusFrenchDraft: Choisir entre vous et tu avec l’hôtesse, son petit-fils et un client âgé, puis formuler des demandes polies.

cards.sourceNoteEnglish: A licensed Cuban family home that rents rooms to travelers.

cards.targetFrenchDraft: la façon de s’adresser à quelqu’un
don (titre de respect avant un prénom)
cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Used before a first name: don Rigoberto. Pair it with usted.
Cuban word for papaya; in Cuba avoid saying papaya.
Softer and more polite than quiero.

cards.sourceSpanish: Marcus, a la señora Odalys háblale de usted.
cards.supportEnglish: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Marcus, adresse-toi à señora Odalys en la vouvoyant.

cards.sourceSpanish: Señora Odalys, ¿me podría servir un poco más de café?
cards.supportEnglish: Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Señora Odalys, pourriez-vous me servir un peu plus de café ?

cards.sourceSpanish: Yandiel, ¿te importa pasarme la fruta bomba?
cards.supportEnglish: Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Yandiel, ça te dérange de me passer la fruta bomba ?
cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Informal: tú with a young person.

cards.sourceSpanish: Don Rigoberto, ¿usted es de aquí, de Trinidad?
cards.supportEnglish: Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Don Rigoberto, êtes-vous d’ici, de Trinidad ?
cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Formal: usted with an older guest.

cards.sourceSpanish: Quisiera otro batido de guayaba, si no es molestia.
cards.supportEnglish: I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Je voudrais un autre batido à la goyave, si ça ne vous dérange pas.
cards.sourceNoteEnglish: Formal and soft; good with the host.

cards.sourceSpanish: Con Yandiel puedes tutearlo, porque nos tuteó primero.
cards.supportEnglish: You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Avec Yandiel, tu peux le tutoyer, puisqu’il nous a tutoyés le premier.

cards.sourceSpanish: Si ella te dice que la tutees, entonces cambias.
cards.supportEnglish: If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: Si elle te dit que tu peux la tutoyer, alors tu changes.

cards.sourceSpanish: Ahora prueba tú: pídele el azúcar a don Rigoberto.
cards.supportEnglish: Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.
cards.targetFrenchDraft: À toi maintenant : demande le sucre à don Rigoberto.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía y su amigo Marcus desayunan en el portal de una casa particular en Trinidad, Cuba.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía and her friend Marcus are having breakfast on the front porch of a casa particular in Trinidad, Cuba.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía et son ami Marcus prennent le petit-déjeuner sous le porche d’une casa particular à Trinidad, à Cuba.

reader.sourceSpanish: La anfitriona, la señora Odalys, pone en la mesa una cafetera de café recién colado.
reader.supportEnglish: The host, señora Odalys, puts a coffee pot of freshly brewed coffee on the table.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: L’hôtesse, señora Odalys, pose sur la table une cafetière de café fraîchement préparé.

reader.sourceSpanish: Marcus no sabe qué trato usar con cada persona de la mesa, así que Lucía le explica la diferencia.
reader.supportEnglish: Marcus doesn't know which way of addressing people to use with each person at the table, so Lucía explains the difference to him.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Marcus ne sait pas comment s’adresser à chacun autour de la table ; Lucía lui explique donc la différence entre le vouvoiement et le tutoiement.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Marcus, a la señora Odalys háblale de usted.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : Marcus, adresse-toi à señora Odalys en la vouvoyant.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Con la dueña de la casa o con una persona mayor, el usted muestra respeto.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: With the owner of the house or with an older person, usted shows respect.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : Avec la propriétaire de la maison ou une personne âgée, le vouvoiement marque le respect.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Si ella te dice que la tutees, entonces cambias.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : Si elle te dit que tu peux la tutoyer, alors tu changes.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luego Lucía da el ejemplo con una pregunta suave: Señora Odalys, ¿me podría servir un poco más de café?
reader.supportEnglish: Then Lucía gives an example with a gentle question: Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Puis Lucía montre comment formuler une demande polie : Señora Odalys, pourriez-vous me servir un peu plus de café ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Yandiel, el nieto de la anfitriona, llega al portal y le pregunta a Marcus: Oye, ¿tú eres americano?
reader.supportEnglish: Yandiel, the host's grandson, comes out to the porch and asks Marcus: Hey, are you American?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Yandiel, le petit-fils de l’hôtesse, arrive sous le porche et demande à Marcus : Hé, tu es américain ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Con Yandiel puedes tutearlo, porque nos tuteó primero.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : Avec Yandiel, tu peux le tutoyer, puisqu’il nous a tutoyés le premier.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Entre jóvenes, el tuteo muestra confianza y no es una falta de respeto.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: Among young people, using tú shows closeness and is not a lack of respect.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : Entre jeunes, le tutoiement exprime la proximité et ne manque pas de respect.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía pone el ejemplo: Yandiel, ¿te importa pasarme la fruta bomba?
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía gives the example: Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía donne un exemple : Yandiel, ça te dérange de me passer la fruta bomba ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Don Rigoberto, un huésped de unos 70 años, sale de su cuarto y se sienta junto a Marcus.
reader.supportEnglish: Don Rigoberto, a guest of about 70, comes out of his room and sits down next to Marcus.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Don Rigoberto, un client d’environ soixante-dix ans, sort de sa chambre et s’assoit à côté de Marcus.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: A un señor mayor que llamas don, también le hablas de usted.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: An older man you call don, you also address with usted.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : À un homme plus âgé que tu appelles don, tu t’adresses aussi en le vouvoyant.

reader.sourceSpanish: Marcus pregunta con cuidado: Don Rigoberto, ¿usted es de aquí, de Trinidad?
reader.supportEnglish: Marcus asks carefully: Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Marcus demande prudemment : Don Rigoberto, êtes-vous d’ici, de Trinidad ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Don Rigoberto sonríe y contesta: No, soy de Cienfuegos, pero vengo cada año a esta casa.
reader.supportEnglish: Don Rigoberto smiles and answers: No, I'm from Cienfuegos, but I come to this house every year.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Don Rigoberto sourit et répond : Non, je suis de Cienfuegos, mais je viens chaque année dans cette maison.

reader.sourceSpanish: Lucía: Ahora prueba tú: pídele el azúcar a don Rigoberto.
reader.supportEnglish: Lucía: Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Lucía : À toi maintenant : demande le sucre à don Rigoberto.

reader.sourceSpanish: Marcus: Don Rigoberto, ¿me podría pasar el azúcar, por favor?
reader.supportEnglish: Marcus: Don Rigoberto, could you pass me the sugar, please?
reader.targetFrenchDraft: Marcus : Don Rigoberto, pourriez-vous me passer le sucre, s’il vous plaît ?

reader.sourceSpanish: Al final, Marcus le dice a la anfitriona con una sonrisa: Quisiera otro batido de guayaba, si no es molestia.
reader.supportEnglish: At the end, Marcus says to the host with a smile: I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.
reader.targetFrenchDraft: À la fin, Marcus dit à l’hôtesse en souriant : Je voudrais un autre batido à la goyave, si ça ne vous dérange pas.

speakingDraft.roleEnglish: You are Lucía coaching Marcus at señora Odalys’s casa particular in Trinidad. The host, grandson Yandiel and guest don Rigoberto also speak.
speakingDraft.openingFrench: Marcus : Lucía, dois-je vouvoyer señora Odalys ?
objectivesEnglish: Explain when Marcus should use French vous or tu, while noting that the Spanish source contrasts usted and tú.
Model a polite coffee request to señora Odalys.
Use tu with Yandiel after he uses tu first and ask him for fruta bomba.
Address don Rigoberto with vous and ask for sugar, then request another guava batido from the host.
speakingDraft.closureFrench: Marcus : Merci, Lucía. Je vais m’adresser à chacun de la manière qui convient.

formsDraft.english: I address señora Odalys with vous.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French vouvoiement adapts the Spanish source’s usted choice; the words are not interchangeable literal translations.

formsDraft.french: Je tutoie Yandiel puisqu’il nous tutoie.
formsDraft.english: I use tu with Yandiel because he uses tu with us.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French tutoiement adapts the source’s tuteo after Yandiel initiates informal address.

formsDraft.french: Pourriez-vous me servir un peu plus de café ?
formsDraft.english: Could you serve me a little more coffee?
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French conditional could softens a request to the host.

formsDraft.french: Ça te dérange de me passer la fruta bomba ?
formsDraft.english: Do you mind passing me the papaya?
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French informal te matches Yandiel’s informal address; fruta bomba retains the source’s Cuban food term.

formsDraft.french: Je voudrais un autre batido à la goyave, si ça ne vous dérange pas.
formsDraft.english: I’d like another guava smoothie, if it’s no trouble.
formsDraft.noteEnglish: French voudrais and vous mark a soft request to the host; batido is retained as a source food term.

reviewNotesEnglish: The source teaches Spanish usted/tú and Cuban address customs; the French target adapts this to vouvoiement/tutoiement. A qualified French/curriculum reviewer must decide how visibly the source-language distinction is taught alongside the French one.
Keep Trinidad, casa particular, señora Odalys, Yandiel, don Rigoberto, Cienfuegos, fruta bomba and batido; the archived Québec/Lavoie/Julien/berries/apple-juice scene is not an equivalent answer.
Qualified French/Cuban locale review should settle borrowed honorifics and food labels, formal versus informal register, and whether client is the best contextual term for the male guest.
Do not generalize the source’s age- and invitation-based address examples into a universal Cuban or French etiquette rule; preserve them as scene dialogue.
Archived card/Reader IDs and audio cannot migrate to these revision-scoped candidates on text overlap alone.
